item.title: Genome Biology: Chemogenomic profiling of diverse Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains using the novel CRISPR-Cas9 markerless barcoded library BarMix
Cell Genomics: TFXcan reveals transcription factor programs driving GWAS loci
item.description: Adeluwa et al. developed TFXcan, a framework that predicts personalized transcription factor binding from genotype data across ∼700 transcription-factor-tissue pairs. Applied to PrCa risk, TFXcan identified specific transcription factors and coordinated programs of transcription factors that drive the disease at risk loci.

item.title: Genome Biology: The glutamine-aspartate metabolic tradeoff between fast growth and metabolic flexibility
Nucleic Acids Research: Microsatellite expansion redirects chromatin modifiers to confer insect resistance to Bt bioinsecticides
item.description: Abstract Microsatellites are highly mutable genomic elements, yet their role in adaptive gene regulation in insects remains poorly understood. Here, we show that a tetranucleotide (ATGT) microsatellite expansion in the promoter of ABCC2 , a key Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) toxin receptor gene, epigenetically silences its expression and confers resistance to Bt Cry1Ac toxin in Plutella xylostella (L.). Mechanistically, long repeats (≥27 units) in Cry1Ac-resistant strains preferentially recruit the histone methyltransferase E(z), promoting H3K27me2/3 deposition, chromatin compaction, and transcriptional silencing, whereas short repeats in susceptible strains maintain open chromatin through Tip60-mediated H4K5 acetylation. This repeat expansion alone is sufficient to repress ABCC2 , thereby conferring Bt resistance, while repeat length, chromatin state, and associated phenotypes partially revert under relaxed selection. These findings define a previously uncharacterized cis -acting element dynamically orchestrating insecticide resistance-associated gene expression and identify microsatellite-driven chromatin remodeling as a general and plastic regulatory strategy underlying rapid xenobiotic-resistance evolution in insects.

item.title: Nucleic Acids Research: Uracil overload triggers global genome instability and dUTPdysgenesis
item.description: Abstract Uracil accumulation in DNA is a pervasive threat to genomic integrity, yet the global dynamics of how uracil overload drives genome instability remain elusive. Using Saccharomyces cerevisiae strains with attenuated dUTPase ( DUT1 ) expression, we mapped the landscapes of genomic alterations including point mutations, recombination, and aneuploidy. Deletion of the UNG1 suppressed most induced mutations and loss-of-heterozygosity (LOH), identifying base excision repair as the primary driver of genomic alterations, whereas aneuploidy directly depends on the persistence of intact genomic uracil. Mechanistically, beyond localized bypass of static AP sites by translesion synthesis polymerases, the massive influx of uracil lesions induces a repair bottleneck by depleting Ung1 and Apn1. This resource titration, coupled with downstream processing intermediates, primarily drives mutagenesis at heterologous nonthymine positions. Furthermore, persistent static AP sites preferentially stimulate homologous recombination sub-pathway that yield interstitial LOH, whereas Apn1-mediated processing channels recombination toward terminal LOH. Crucially, we define a novel post-zygotic isolation mechanism, dUTPdysgenesis, where parental wild-type Ung1 unleashes an immediate enzymatic shock against a uracil-preloaded genome upon mating, triggering G1-phase chromosomal shattering and mutations. Collectively, this study transitions the paradigm of uracil mutagenesis from localized errors to a global engine of genome instability, bridging nucleotide metabolism, DNA repair kinetics, and speciation barriers.

item.title: Genome Biology: Urbanisation drives parallel genomic divergence across cities and bumble bee species
Genome Biology: Mitonuclear control of transcription complexes regulates tRNA splicing
Nucleic Acids Research: Structural basis for coupled DNA replication and uracil repair by a family of DNA polymerases from phages with T-modified genomes
item.description: Abstract Replicative DNA polymerases (DNAPs) play a critical role in genome duplication, ensuring the accurate transmission of genetic information in all domains of life. DNAPs are also essential for DNA viruses, as well as bacteriophages, where a uracil-DNA glycosylase (UDG) is often encoded in trans or is present in the DNAP gene. Here, we identify a new group of A-family DNAPs in phages that are fused to an active UDG domain and contain other large insertions. Several members of this subfamily, including phages SP-15 and YerA41, are known to be hypermodified on their thymidine base through glycosylation of a linker attached to the C5 position of thymine. We determined the atomic cryo-EM structures for two of its members in various active functional and conformational states, from YerA41 and phiLo phages. The structures reveal how these large DNAPs function as replicative DNAPs, and how they can recognize dU bases ahead of the replication fork through their UDG domain, generating abasic sites that are preferentially bypassed through dA incorporation. Such dU errors would need to be eliminated to preserve phage genome integrity. Additionally, we report the co-occurrence of both an X-family DNAP and a DNA ligase in the corresponding phage genomes and show that both enzymes can execute the final steps of base excision repair most probably on-the-fly during replication, revealing a DNA-replication-coupled repair process. The structures of these large polymerases can serve as a model of other large platform DNAPs that can recruit additional enzymatic activities necessary for phage or virus survival.

item.title: Nucleic Acids Research: Neuronal DNA repair mediates systemic mitochondrial maintenance through acetylcholine signaling
item.description: Abstract DNA repair defects such as nucleotide excision repair (NER) mutations can lead to progeroid syndromes characterized by growth retardation and accelerated aging with distinct tissue type specific pathologies. DNA-damage-induced dysfunction of specific cell types can impair the organism’s overall function. It is unknown whether, in reverse, DNA repair in specific tissues can have non-cell-autonomous consequences on other tissues carrying DNA damage. To explore the organismal consequences of cell-type-specific DNA repair, we restricted NER activity to specific tissues and monitored consequences on organismal health in Caenorhabditis elegans . Unexpectedly, we observed that tissue-specific DNA repair is sufficient to improve overall DNA damage resistance. Strikingly, NER activity restricted to neurons only is sufficient to provide similar overall DNA damage resistance as whole-body NER in almost all tissues tested. We show that this systemic DNA damage resilience is mediated by neuronal acetylcholine signaling that promotes the maintenance of mitochondrial activity throughout the organism.

item.title: Nucleic Acids Research: Condensins-mediated mitotic folding persists as a structural echo in interphase chromatin
item.description: Abstract The structural maintenance of chromosomes (SMC) protein complexes, cohesin and condensins, orchestrate cell cycle-dependent transitions in chromosome folding: from the relatively decondensed interphase chromatin, organized into dynamic DNA loops by cohesin, to the highly condensed arrays of DNA loops in mitotic chromosomes formed by condensins. Here, using Hi-C data from mouse embryonic stem cell lines with auxin-inducible degron-tagged subunits of SMC complexes, we clarify the role of condensins in shaping chromatin contacts within the interphase nucleus. We found that depletion of condensin I leads to weakened segregation of chromatin into A and B compartments. We also show that the contact patterns established by condensins during mitosis are preserved in interphase, suggesting a structural memory of mitotic chromosome folding. Condensins influence chromocenter organization: in the absence of condensin II during mitosis, centromeres tend to cluster, forming hyperclusters of pericentric heterochromatin. In contrast, depletion of condensin I reduces the number of heterochromatin clusters, consistent with enhanced chromosome territoriality. By combining a cohesin-degron system with Mcph1 knockout, we established an artificial model in which condensin II becomes the major driver of chromatin folding in interphase nuclei following cohesin depletion. Unlike extrusive cohesin, condensin II does not stall at sequence-specific sites and forms large, randomly positioned loops on interphase chromatin. Moreover, condensin II activity during interphase does not interfere with cohesin-dependent structures such as TADs and chromatin loops.

item.title: Nucleic Acids Research: E. coli RsmF activity depends on prior modification of 16S rRNA helix 44
item.description: Abstract Bacterial ribosomal RNA (rRNA) methylations are important for accurate translation. Four distinct methylations incorporated by RsmE, RsmF, and RsmH/ RsmI form a cluster of three modified 16S rRNA nucleotides (m 3 U1498, m 5 C1407, and m 4 Cm1402) surrounding the decoding center of the 30S subunit. Given their common substrate requirement of a late-stage intermediate 30S subunit, these enzymes likely act contemporaneously during subunit biogenesis, but whether there exists a required modification order is unknown. Here, using hypomethylated 30S subunits obtained from a collection of rsmH/I/E/F -deleted Escherichia coli strains, we identify RsmF activity to be highly dependent on prior modification of h44 both in vitro and in E. coli . RsmF activity on hypomethylated 30S subunits could be partially rescued by prior in vitro methylation using RsmE and RsmH, indicating that incorporation of these methyl groups directly shapes h44 for recognition by RsmF. RNA structure probing using selective 2′-hydroxyl acylation analyzed by primer extension and mutational profiling and molecular dynamics simulations reveal specific alterations in 16S rRNA structure and dynamics in the absence of the m 4 C1402 (RsmH) and m 3 U1498 (RsmE) modifications that likely restrict RsmF action. These studies thus uncover a previously unappreciated “order of operations” for 16S rRNA modification during ribosome biogenesis with important implications for studies on the collective functions of these modifications.

item.title: Nature Genetics: High false sign rates in transcriptome-wide association studies
item.description: This study finds that the direction of effect captured by transcriptome-wide association studies is often reversed relative to the true biological mechanism, suggesting that caution is needed when interpreting these studies and using the results for downstream applications.

item.title: Nature Genetics: Near-complete assembly of wild emmer wheat unveils centromere reorganization during polyploid evolution
item.description: A near-complete genome assembly of wild emmer wheat with resolved centromeric regions across 14 chromosomes highlights subgenome-associated patterns of centromere remodeling during wheat polyploid evolution.

item.title: Nature Genetics: Establishing Polycomb regulatory landscapes in human early development
item.description: The authors profile H2AK119ub (H2Aub) in human gametes, two-cell embryos, eight-cell embryos, blastocysts and human embryonic stem cells. Their analysis provides a comprehensive view of H2Aub reprogramming and patterning during the earliest stages of human development.

item.title: Cell Genomics: NeoBridge: Biophysics-informed neoantigen prioritization and clonal architecture profiling in pancreatic cancer
item.description: Lana Mediavilla et al. present NeoBridge, a biophysics-informed machine learning ensemble that prioritizes immunogenic neoantigens. In pancreatic cancer, subclonal neoantigen load, not clonal load, associates with worse survival, suggesting that clonal architecture should inform vaccine target selection

item.title: Cell Genomics: Detecting low-allele-fraction mosaic mutations: A multi-institution benchmarking with cell-line mixtures
item.description: Ha et al. benchmark detection strategies for mosaic mutations with low variant allele fractions (VAFs) using short- and long-read whole-genome sequencing. By cross-validating Illumina-based calls against PacBio HiFi data using cell-line mixtures generated across five institutions, they construct stratified reference sets, define realistic detection limits, and establish best practices for genome-wide analysis of low-VAF (<2%) variants in non-cancer tissues.

item.title: Cell Genomics: A pangenomic method for establishing a synthetic somatic variant resource in HapMap mixtures
item.description: Kong et al. present a comprehensive resource for benchmarking somatic variant detection across variant classes and allele fractions. Using HapMap mixtures and pangenome graphs, they establish standardized benchmarking sets for evaluating sequencing technologies and variant-calling methods.

item.title: Genome Biology: A new phased assembly of the Antarctic spiny plunderfish provides novel insights into the evolution of the notothenioid radiation
Genome Biology: The contribution of short tandem repeats to splicing variation in the human prefrontal cortex
Genome Biology: ROMET-RNA benchmarks and selects RNA 3D structures using multiple predictors and alignment strategies
Genome Biology: Germline structural variation involving gynecologic and breast cancers reveals polygenic signatures of tumor mutational load
Genome Biology: Commensal Lachnospiraceae bacterium mitigates colitis-induced mucin fucosylation deficits through ILC3/IL-22 axis
Genome Biology: Extensive admixture and introgression shape genetic diversity and evolutionary adaptation in indigenous East Asian cattle
Genome Biology: Dynamic landscapes of gene regulatory networks during early mammalian neurogenesis for understanding brain evolution and disorder risk
Genome Biology: Benchmarking long-read aligner-caller pipelines for structural variant detection across ten angiosperm species with PacBio high-fidelity sequencing
Genome Biology: Non-invasive genomic sampling uncovers novel connectivities and origins of confiscated gorillas
Cell Genomics: Choice of phenotype scale is critical in biobank-based G × E tests
item.description: Phenotype measurement scale has long been known to impact genetic inference, yet it is often ignored in modern studies. Costantino et al. characterize how the choice of phenotype scale affects the results of common analyses. They find that it can change GWAS hits and PGS × E interactions and influence PGS performance in specific subgroups.

item.title: Genome Biology: Poison exon splicing in the human brain provides a new paradigm for understanding and targeting neurological disorders
Nature Genetics: Clonal heterogeneity in human pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma and its impact on tumor progression
item.description: This study uses single-cell RNA sequencing and spatial transcriptomics of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma tumors to investigate tumor heterogeneity and clonal evolution, providing a valuable resource for this aggressive cancer.

item.title: Genome Biology: Hi-C derived insulation strength predicts evolutionary conservation of topologically associating domains
Nature Genetics: Micronuclear ecDNA constrains tumor cell fitness and is associated with favorable patient survival
item.description: Single-micronucleus sequencing and live-cell imaging of cancer cells, as well as analyses of biopsies from patients with neuroblastoma, reveal that ecDNA in micronuclei limits tumor cell fitness and is associated with patient survival.

item.title: Genome Biology: Surface proteomics reveals arginine metabolism as a vulnerability in high grade serous ovarian cancer
Genome Biology: Integrating physiological and proteomics signatures for understanding drought, salinity and alkalinity stress tolerance mechanisms in lentil
Genome Biology: Identification of regulators of aryl hydrocarbon receptor signaling in human cells by genome-scale CRISPR screening
Nature Genetics: Imputation of fluid intelligence scores reduces ascertainment bias and increases power for analyses of common and rare variants
item.description: Imputing unmeasured fluid intelligence scores in UK Biobank reduces ascertainment bias and increases power for genetic analyses, improving out-of-sample polygenic score performance and identifying rare variant signals that are strongly enriched for intellectual disability-associated genes.

item.title: Nature Genetics: A heritability-optimized method for functional prioritization of rare coding variants in complex traits
item.description: This study presents RovHer, a heritability-optimized scoring method for estimating the functional impact of rare variants, which is applied to the UK Biobank to demonstrate its ability to enrich for missense rare variants that maximally explain complex trait heritability.

item.title: Genome Biology: A curated genome-scale nucleotide diversity panel of non-human primates
Nature Genetics: Single-allele nanoscale mapping of regulatory variants
item.description: This study uses high-resolution, allele-specific chromatin architecture to identify causal gene-regulatory mechanisms in inflammatory diseases and uncovers a mechanism by which a neo-CTCF site promotes autoimmunity.

item.title: Nature Genetics: Reactivation of the embryonic ζ-globin gene ameliorates severe forms of α-thalassemia
item.description: Liu et al. identify cis -regulatory elements that silence the embryonic ζ-globin gene in definitive erythroid cells. Gene-editing strategies reactivate ζ-globin expression to therapeutically relevant levels in mouse and human disease models.

item.title: Genome Biology: Landscape and mutational dynamics of G-quadruplexes across the complete human genome
Genome Biology: Autumn–winter progression triggers distinct transcriptional programs in Arabidopsis thaliana
Nature Genetics: Single-cell profiling and genetic regulation of alternative polyadenylation in the human brain
item.description: This study provides a single-cell atlas of 3′ untranslated region regulation in the human brain, pointing to molecular mechanisms for genetic variants contributing to Alzheimer’s disease, Parkinson’s disease and other brain disorders beyond gene expression.

item.title: Nature Genetics: Lineage identity governs oncogene dependence in mouse NSCLC models of KRAS inhibitor resistance
item.description: KRAS-mutant lung cancers frequently develop resistance to targeted inhibition. This study demonstrates that lineage plasticity shapes oncogene dependence during response and resistance to KRAS inhibition, establishing new models of histologic transformation.

item.title: Nature Genetics: CCNB1IP1 regulatory evolution underlies gradual increases in cortical size and folding in primates
item.description: The authors use tree shrews in multispecies comparisons to identify evolutionary changes in CCNB1IP1 expression associated with primate cortical expansion and folding, and investigate the cis -regulatory and molecular mechanisms through which CCNB1IP1 may influence these processes.

item.title: Cell Genomics: Disease-associated loci share properties with response eQTLs under common environmental exposures
item.description: Lin and Li et al. expose differentiating human stem cell cultures to nicotine, caffeine, or ethanol and identify genetic variants whose effects on gene expression emerge only after exposure. These context-specific regulatory variants resemble disease-associated loci, illustrating how environment-sensitive gene regulation can help explain signals from human genetic studies.

item.title: Nature Genetics: A human single-cell atlas identifies OLR1 + scar-associated macrophages as a potential therapeutic target for chronic liver disease
item.description: This study provides a single-cell RNA-sequencing atlas of 77 healthy and chronic liver disease livers and identifies a subpopulation of pro-inflammatory scar-associated macrophages enriched for OLR1 expression with therapeutic potential.

item.title: Nature Genetics: Germline homologous recombination deficiency influences TP53 -mutant clonal hematopoiesis fitness during platinum and PARP inhibitor treatment
item.description: The authors show that platinum is a greater driver of DNA damage response gene-mutant clonal hematopoiesis than poly(ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitors and that the presence of germline mutations conferring homologous recombination deficiency reduces the rate of expansion of these clones.

item.title: Cell Genomics: Single-cell multiomics across nine mammals reveals cell-type-specific regulatory conservation in the brain
item.description: Anderson et al. compare brain gene regulation across nine mammals, revealing that enhancer conservation extends beyond DNA sequence to include cell-type specificity and gene targets. Functional assays show how both ancient and human-specific regulatory elements shape brain biology and susceptibility to neurologic disease.

item.title: Genome Biology: Spatial and single-nucleus transcriptomics reveal the complexity of genomic imprinting in maize
Nature Genetics: Single-cell analysis of chromatin accessibility in the human intestine identifies regulatory programs and clarifies genetic associations in Crohn’s disease
item.description: This study uses single-cell ATAC–seq to map chromatin accessibility in the intestinal mucosa from patients with Crohn’s disease and healthy controls to characterize regulatory programs associated with inflammation and genetic effects.

item.title: Nature Genetics: Genome-wide mapping of common and rare variant effects on adiposity across childhood
item.description: Genome-wide analyses identify common and rare variants associated with childhood adiposity, including rare protein-coding variants in ADCY3 , CALCR , MC4R , MRAP2 , POMC and MYH13 that exhibit stronger effects in children than in adults.

item.title: Nature Genetics: Euchromatin forms condensed domains with short active regions on the surface
item.description: Simulations integrating micro-C and imaging data provide a coherent view of chromatin organization from nucleosomes to clutches to domains, revealing that most regions form compact domains but short regulatory elements are highly exposed.

item.title: Nature Genetics: Atlas of cell types and regulatory elements underlying human facial diversity
item.description: Single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics and chromatin accessibility maps of the human craniofacial region in developing embryos provide insights into the mechanisms underlying facial variation and pathology.

item.title: Nature Genetics: Divergent medulloblastoma chromatin states disclose KDM2B as a selective dependency
item.description: Epigenomic analyses of medulloblastoma identify a bivalent/poised enhancer (EnhBiv) chromatin signature enriched for KDM2B binding in Group 3 and Group 4 tumors. Functional work suggests a selective dependency of these subtypes on KDM2B.

item.title: Genome Biology: The trajectory of KoRV-A evolution suggests initial integration into the koala germline genome near Coffs Harbour in New South Wales
Nature Genetics: Genetic factor analysis for characterizing phenome-wide patterns of genetic pleiotropy
item.description: Genetic factor analysis uses genome-wide association summary statistics to identify shared polygenic factors underlying patterns of cross-trait genetic associations, while automatically determining the number of factors and accounting for sample overlap.

item.title: Genome Biology: The Onychomys pangenome reveals the unique molecular adaptations that confer toxin resistance
Genome Research: Multilevel ensemble for genome-wide prediction of cell-specific G-quadruplexes utilizing transformed sequences and enhanced chromatin accessibility with G4Beacon2
Cell Genomics: Concentrating cell-type-specific transcriptional signatures in bone marrow from interspecies comparisons
item.description: The authors present a framework to isolate condensed marker gene signatures by requiring both conserved cell-type specificity and conserved expression across multi-species scRNA-seq datasets. Bone marrow niche and hematopoietic progenitor signatures from four mouse species robustly resolve cell identity in two outgroup primate species, capturing highly conserved, biologically meaningful information.

item.title: Cell Genomics: Pre-diagnosis plasma cell-free DNA reveals early signatures of prostate and breast cancer risk up to eight years prior to clinical detection
item.description: Cheng et al. profile genome-wide cfDNA methylation in archived, prospectively collected plasma sampled 2 weeks to 9 years before breast or prostate cancer diagnosis. Regulatory-element signatures stratify future prostate cancer risk and reveal modest, heterogeneous breast cancer signals that vary by subtype, mammography interval, and progression to metastatic disease.

item.title: Genome Biology: Transcriptomic efficiency shapes growth-defense trade-offs in alpine desert plants under climate change
Genome Biology: Structural variants contribute substantially to complex trait heritability
Genome Research: CircExor enables interpretable prediction of circRNA localization into extracellular vesicles
Cell Genomics: Mutation timing, accumulation, and selection in the male germline shape inheritance risk for developmental disorders
item.description: Neville et al. combine trio whole-genome sequencing with ultra-accurate sperm sequencing to quantify how de novo mutation timing and selection shape transmittable disease risk. Early embryonic mosaicism can create an uncommon elevated transmission risk, whereas universal age-associated mutation accumulation and spermatogonial selection account for most paternal pathogenic de novo mutations.

RNA: Seed pairing between a small regulatory RNA and target mRNA determines cleavage by an RNase E with a minimal C-terminal scaffold
Genome Research: Nuclear mitochondrial sequences in great ape telomere-to-telomere genomes
Cell Genomics: Single-library chromosome-scale diploid assemblies of vole genomes resolve a species-specific duplication implicated in pair bonding
item.description: Abuelanin et al. combine PacBio HiFi with low-coverage CiFi proximity-ligation reads in a single library and sequencing run to generate contiguous, near-telomere-to-telomere, accurately phased diploid genomes of prairie and meadow voles. These assemblies reveal strikingly rapid genome evolution, including near-complete Y chromosome divergence and a prairie-vole-specific Avpr1a duplication implicated in pair bonding.

Genome Research: Characterizing intra- and intertumor heterogeneity in ovarian high-grade serous carcinoma subtypes using single-cell and spatial transcriptomics

RNA: Contributions of folded and disordered domains to RNA binding by HNRNPR
